subsystems.name: Sensor element
subsystems.role: converts a physical quantity — temperature, pressure, motion, trace gases — into an electrical signal.

subsystems.name: Node electronics
subsystems.role: processes readings and drives the radio in a package a few millimetres across.

subsystems.name: Power source
subsystems.role: keeps a chip-scale node alive for months without maintenance.

subsystems.name: Dispersion platform
subsystems.role: releases very large numbers of nodes across a target region at a chosen altitude.

subsystems.name: Mesh and backhaul
subsystems.role: moves readings from isolated drifting nodes to the internet.

subsystems.name: Data layer
subsystems.role: fuses billions of intermittent streams into a usable picture of a region or the planet.

buildSteps.title: Design the node
buildSteps.detail: Chip-scale co-design of sensor, radio, power and packaging within a target volume of a few cubic millimetres, with an energy budget that dictates how often it can sense and transmit.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the wafers
buildSteps.detail: MEMS structures and CMOS circuits are made on standard semiconductor lines, since no new physics is needed — only extreme miniaturisation and yield control.

buildSteps.title: Add power and encapsulation
buildSteps.detail: Thin-film batteries or tiny harvesters are attached, then the node is sealed in a casing engineered to dissolve after a set exposure to rain, sunlight and microbes.

buildSteps.title: Assemble at volume
buildSteps.detail: Panel-level or roll-to-roll packaging places billions of nodes per year at a cost low enough that losing most of them is acceptable.

buildSteps.title: Disperse
buildSteps.detail: Balloons, aircraft or drones release batches of nodes over the target area, relying on wind to spread them; each node falls slowly and begins reporting on landing or while airborne.

buildSteps.title: Self-organise
buildSteps.detail: Nodes discover neighbours, form multi-hop routes and forward readings toward whichever gateway or satellite pass is cheapest in energy.

buildSteps.title: Backhaul and fuse
buildSteps.detail: Gateways and satellites relay data to data centres, where streams are quality-checked, geolocated and merged into continuous fields.

buildSteps.title: Model and act
buildSteps.detail: The fused field feeds weather prediction, disaster warning and climate monitoring — the actual purpose of the network.

buildSteps.title: Degrade and account
buildSteps.detail: Nodes break down on schedule; operators track material mass balance so that what is dispersed does not accumulate in soils, water or food chains.

prerequisites.why: MEMS sensors and low-power radios are everywhere, but combining sensing, radio and power in a sub-millimetre drifting package has not been demonstrated.

prerequisites.tech: Wireless mesh networking at extreme scale
prerequisites.why: meshes of thousands of fixed nodes work; trillions of moving, power-starved nodes would need routing and spectrum schemes that do not yet exist.

prerequisites.tech: Ambient energy harvesting at millimetre scale
prerequisites.why: tiny solar cells and thermal harvesters work, but not at the power density needed for constant sensing plus radio transmission.
dissolvable silicon and biodegradable substrates have been shown in labs for medical implants, not for millions of tonnes of environmental hardware.
satellite links for small devices exist, but bandwidth and coverage are far below what a planetary mesh would generate.
the semiconductor and display industries already make billions of devices a year at very low unit cost.

pathway.milestone: coarse coverage from static ground networks, ocean drifters and Earth-observation satellites
pathway.unlocks: regional weather forecasting and disaster monitoring, with large gaps over oceans and sparsely instrumented land.

pathway.milestone: denser airborne and drifting sensors — more weather balloons, ocean drifters and high-altitude platforms, including short-lived disposable ones
pathway.unlocks: better data over the roughly two-thirds of the planet that is ocean.

pathway.milestone: controlled-release micro-node swarms over a bounded test region, with full recovery or degradation accounting
pathway.unlocks: evidence on cost, lifetime, spectrum use and environmental impact before any wider release.

pathway.milestone: continental-scale mesh feeding a continuously updated digital model of the surface and atmosphere
pathway.unlocks: faster hazard warning and better-constrained climate projections.

pathway.milestone: a genuinely planet-wide mesh, if energy, communication, material lifetime and ecological questions are all answered
pathway.unlocks: the stated goal of dense global sensing — though 'every square metre' remains a physical and environmental limit, not just an engineering one.
